Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.

# Intake Brief: Follow-on-Steam incentive — unlock a bundled free game in the Steam launcher

## Problem statement

The upcoming Steam release of the Tableau Card Engine launcher (Electron) needs a growth mechanic: when a player follows the game/developer on Steam, they receive one of the bundled example games for free. The mechanic must feel seamless — the Steam store page opens automatically (player already logged in), they follow, and the launcher detects the follow and unlocks the bonus game.

## Users

- **Steam players** — get a free game as an incentive to follow the TCE Steam presence; discover the engine's games.
- **TCE developers/publisher** — grow Steam following/wishlists and reward engaged players without manual key distribution.

**User stories:**
- As a Steam player, I want to click "Follow us on Steam" in the launcher and have the store page open automatically (already logged in), so following takes one click.
- As a Steam player, I want the bonus game to unlock in my launcher once I've followed, so I can play it immediately.
- As a publisher, I want the free-game unlock to be delivered through the existing bundled-content/DLC architecture, so no manual key handling is needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The launcher shows a "Follow us on Steam" call-to-action (e.g. a small panel/button) that opens the game's Steam store page in the Steam client/overlay via Steamworks (player is already logged in — no browser login prompt).
2. After the player follows, the launcher detects the follow via Steamworks and unlocks the designated bonus game (one of the existing example games) in the launcher's game list; verified by an end-to-end check with a real Steam account (manual QA) and, where feasible, a mocked Steamworks session in automated tests.
3. The unlock persists across launches (player who followed once keeps the game; no re-verification prompt on every boot).
4. The bonus game is delivered as part of the bundled-content architecture (locked by default) so no separate download is needed; the unlock mechanism is game-agnostic (works for whichever game is designated as the bonus).
5. If the Steam client/Steamworks is unavailable (e.g. dev environment, non-Steam launch), the launcher must not crash: the CTA degrades gracefully (hidden or "follow via browser" fallback) and the web app remains fully functional.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (`npm test`) and `npm run build` must succeed (quality gate).

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is excluded from this list — it is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **Electron** launcher per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW; this feature integrates Steamworks SDK into that launcher (explicitly deferred scope of the launcher item — this item introduces it).
- **Bonus game is bundled** (answer to intake Q: "a game currently in the example games", delivered via the bundled/subset content in the launcher, unlocked in place) — not a separate download.
- **Steam store page via Steamworks** (intake Q3): the CTA opens the store page in the Steam client; follow detection must use the Steamworks SDK and/or Steam Web API.
- **Licensing:** all code MIT-compatible; no proprietary or copyleft dependencies.
- **Quality gates:** `npm test` and `npm run build` must pass before pushing (project policy).
- **Doc-update policy:** infra/tooling changes require `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and `AGENTS.md` updates (or a tracked child work item).
- **Game-agnostic:** the unlock logic must not hard-code the specific bonus game title (the designated game is a business decision, see Appendix).

## Existing state

- Launcher item CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (intake_complete) delivers the Electron binary that boots the Vite web app; scope explicitly defers Steamworks SDK integration ("No Steamworks SDK integration in v1. The launcher must not require Steam to run locally during development.").
- Launcher content-loading is designed so Steam DLC directories can be read (option a) with structure permitting later Steamworks-managed paths (option b) without a rewrite — the follow-unlock must slot into this abstraction.
- The web app (Game Selector) currently lists all example games; the launcher will bundle a subset.
- No Steamworks SDK, Steam app ID, or Steam-related code exists in the repo today.

## Desired change

1. Add Steamworks SDK integration to the Electron launcher (init/restart-app-if-needed, Steam app ID bootstrap), keeping the launcher runnable without Steam during development.
2. Add a "Follow us on Steam" CTA (in launcher UI, e.g. Game Selector screen or settings) that opens the game's Steam store page in the Steam client — candidate mechanisms: `SteamFriends()->ActivateGameOverlayToStore(appId, ...)` in the Steamworks SDK, or `steam://openurl`/`steam://store/<appid>` external URL from Electron.
3. Detect the follow and unlock the bonus game. **Research required:** Steam's client SDK has no direct "user follows this game's store page" call; candidates to verify during implementation:
   - `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(<developer account steamID>)` — client-side check that the user follows the *developer/publisher account* (works without a backend).
   - Steam Web API (`IPlayerService` family, e.g. followed-games queries) — verifies game-page follows but needs a server component and publisher API key.
   - Whichever mechanism is chosen must be verified against the actual Steam account model (game-page follow vs developer-account follow) before committing.
4. Unlock persistence: store a local unlock flag (or Steam-follow state) so the player isn't re-prompted; re-check on demand (e.g. "Refresh" or on follow confirmation).
5. Graceful degradation when Steam/Steamworks is absent: CTA hidden or browser fallback; web app unaffected.
6. Tests + docs: mock Steamworks session for automated unlock-logic tests where feasible; manual end-to-end QA with a real Steam account documented in the test plan.

## Key Files

- `electron/main.ts` (new) — Steamworks init, Steam app ID bootstrap, store-page open handler, follow-check orchestration.
- `electron/steam-follow.ts` (new) — follow detection + unlock persistence logic (game-agnostic), behind a small interface so the web renderer doesn't depend on the Steam SDK directly.
- `electron/preload.ts` (new) — expose a minimal follow/unlock API to the renderer via context bridge.
- `src/ui/` or launcher UI module — "Follow us on Steam" CTA component (SLL-compliant placement), unlock state display.
- `package.json` — Steamworks SDK dependency (or native module) and scripts; electron-builder config for the Steam distribution.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md`, `README.md`, `RELEASE.md` — document the Steamworks build/QA workflow.
- `AGENTS.md` — note new scripts/requirements if tooling changes.
- `tests/` — unit tests for unlock/persistence logic with a mocked follow source; manual E2E test plan for real-Steam verification.

## Related work

- **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW – Electron launcher for a Steam-ready binary release** (open, intake_complete) — prerequisite: the launcher this feature extends. Its AC #4 (DLC/content-location architecture) must be honored; this feature introduces the deferred Steamworks scope.
- `docs/the-build/genre-research.md` — card-game genre research incl. Steam platform notes (context only).
- No other Steam/Steamworks work items exist (verified via `wl search steam`, `steamworks`, `DLC`).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** The Steam app (App ID) and developer/publisher Steam account exist outside this repo; this item integrates with them.
- **Assumption:** The designated bonus game is a business decision (TBD — see Appendix) and does not change the technical design (game-agnostic unlock).
- **Assumption:** Following is checked once (on CTA completion) and persisted locally; unfollow-after-unlock is not detected/penalised in v1 (anti-abuse is out of scope).
- **Risk (HIGH):** Steam's client SDK may not expose a reliable client-side "followed this game page" check. Mitigation: implementation begins with a short research spike (candidate APIs above); fallback is developer-account follow via `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing`, or a small web-API verification if acceptable. This may change the UX (e.g. follow developer account instead of game page) — confirm with user before committing to a fallback.
- **Risk:** Steamworks native module adds build complexity to electron-builder packaging and must not break non-Steam dev runs — mitigated by graceful-degradation AC (AC5).
- **Risk:** Electron + Steamworks native module (Steam SDK) packaging on Windows must be validated (steam_appid.txt, app id bootstrap, `SteamAPI_RestartAppIfNecessary`).
- **Scope-creep risk:** Steam overlay for achievements, wishlist prompts, key-distribution systems, and anti-abuse (unfollow detection) are out of scope; record as follow-up work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Which game is being released on Steam? The TCE is an engine — are we releasing a specific game built on it (e.g., Main Street), or is this about the engine itself?" — Answer (user): "A launcher with a subset of the example games bundled and the ability to add more later (DLC)." Source: interactive reply. Implication: the Steam "release" is the launcher product (per CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW); this item is a mechanic in that launcher.
- Q2: "What's the 'free game' offer? When a player follows, they receive a free game — is that a specific existing game from the TCE catalog, a bonus game, or something else?" — Answer (user): "it will be a game currently in the example games." Source: interactive reply. The specific game title is **not yet chosen (OPEN QUESTION for the business)**; ACs are game-agnostic.
- Q3: "How does the Steam integration work: store page with follow-to-unlock via Steamworks API, manual key-claim flow, or something else?" — Answer (user): "Steam store page via Steamworks." Source: interactive reply.
- Q4: "What platform does the launcher target?" — Answer (user): "desktop (we will be using electron, another item covers this, add requirements there if necessary, see CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW)". Source: interactive reply. Decision: Electron stack already scoped in CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW; no requirements added to that item (its scope explicitly defers Steamworks — this feature introduces it and is linked as dependent).
- Q5: "What does 'follow us on Steam' mean technically? Steam has no direct follow webhook..." (options: web flow with in-game store open + API check; code redemption; community group) — Answer (user): "I have played a game that automatically opened the steam store page, I was already logged in and I was following the page. I don't know how they did it, but that's what I want." Source: interactive reply. This is the target UX; the exact Steamworks mechanism is a research spike for implementation (see Risks). Likely components: `ActivateGameOverlayToStore` (or `steam://store/<appid>`) to open the page + a follow-state check.
- OPEN QUESTION: Which example game is the designated free follow-bonus? (business decision; doesn't block technical design — AC4 is game-agnostic.)
- OPEN QUESTION: Follow verification mechanism — game-page follow (needs Steam Web API / backend) vs developer-account follow (`ISteamFriends::IsFollowing`, client-side). Must be researched and confirmed with user before implementation commits to a fallback.

## Related work (automated find-related report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MSI4IP6A000N7YF** – Coloretto: align player collections (hands) regardless of name/score length (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated game feature)*.
- **CG-0MQH81RIS0017K94** – Coloretto Phaser scene (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated)*.
- **CG-0MROXIJZ3004VGUI** – GymTokenPileView: card-back pile shows 'not found' texture (completed) — *weak match (generic keyword overlap; unrelated)*.

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-...` — the draft itself (self-match).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (+ a worktree copy) — generic terms (game, feature, store); context only, no Steam-specific content.

> Note: The genuinely related item **CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW** (Electron launcher) is covered in the manual Related work section above.

# Staff job-applicant specialization mechanic

## Problem statement

Main Street currently has a single staff mechanic: staff cards that go into the player's hand and passively expand hand capacity (`handSlotsAdded`). There is no in-game staff that is employed at a specific deployed business and grants that business a passive specialization buff. This item adds that new staff mechanic.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — wants more meaningful decisions when hiring staff: choosing where to place an applicant, weighing passive buffs, and taking on per-turn salary costs.
- **Game designer** — wants a reusable, deterministic staff-applicant mechanic that works with existing staff templates and can be extended with new applicant cards later.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Applicant trigger:** Each turn there is a per-turn chance that a staff member applies for work at one of the deployed businesses on the street. The chance is computed as `(reputation + income per turn)%`, capped at 15%. The applicant targets a deployed business that has a free employment slot (one staff slot per business level).
2. **Passive specialization buff:** Each staff member grants a passive, always-on buff to the business at which they are employed. Skills are assigned from a specialization pool and are randomized **once per game** at game start, remaining locked for the full game; a staff member's skill is disconnected from its nominal job (e.g. a "Baker" can carry a "Town Gossip" skill). At a minimum the "Town Gossip" skill is implemented, firing the existing once-per-turn peek mechanic (see CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN).
3. **Hire / decline flow:** The applicant is presented as a new card type that **walks on from the left** of the screen. The player either lets it walk off to the right (decline) or hires it (walks into the hand / is employed). Hiring costs **no immediate coins** but adds an ongoing per-turn salary cost (deducted alongside existing staff/community-space ongoing costs during the income phase, clamped at 0 coins).
4. **Capacity & let-go economics:** A business can employ one staff member per business level (level 1 = 1 slot, etc.). The player can let a staff member go (lay off), which costs 1 turn's salary and 1 reputation.
5. **Tests & docs:** The mechanic is covered by unit tests (deterministic trigger under seeded RNG, passive-buff application, hire/decline, let-go penalties, per-level slot enforcement) and a browser/scene test for the walk-on/walk-off presentation. All related documentation is updated (code comments, README/wiki docs entries as applicable). Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Staff applicants for this mechanic are **distinct** from the existing hand-slot staff cards (`handSlotsAdded` mechanic) — they do not go into the player's hand as hand cards; they are employed at a deployed business.
- Applicant pool starts from existing staff templates; add new applicant cards via the follow-up work item CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK (not scope here).
- Passive buffs are applied per-business; must not conflict with existing per-slot `currentIncome` / `currentReputationPerTurn` caching in `applyIncome`.
- New card presentation must follow SLL positioning and the shared HandView/PileView / animation + SFX conventions per AGENTS.md (rule 8, `COMMON_SFX_KEYS`, reduced-motion respected).

## Existing state

- `StaffCard` interface in `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` (familly: 'staff') with `handSlotsAdded`, `reputationPerTurn`, `refreshCostDiscount`, `actionsPerTurn`. Staff templates loaded from `card-data.csv` (`_STAFF_CARD_TEMPLATES`).
- `MainStreetState.ts`: `streetGrid` of deployed businesses/community-spaces; `staffCards[]` (hand-slot staff) + `staffCardMarket[]`; business cards carry `maxLevel`/`level`.
- `MainStreetEngine.ts`: `hireStaffCard()` (hand-slot hire), `layOffStaffCard()` (hand-slot layoff), `executeDayStart()` resets per-turn state; `applyIncome()` in `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` deducts staff + community-space ongoing costs and applies per-slot income/rep.
- Related peek skill work: CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN (implement staff peek skill), CG-0MSXOWLHU0099QF6 (face-down deck rendering).

## Desired change

Introduce a per-turn staff-applicant phase/step in the turn loop: roll the applicant chance, when triggered pick a deployed business with a free employment slot and spawn an applicant card that walks on from the left. On hire, employ the applicant at that business, add its passive specialization buff to the business's income/rep/synergy computations, and register its ongoing salary cost. On decline, walk the card off to the right with no effect. Add per-level employment-slot tracking, and a let-go action costing 1 turn's salary + 1 reputation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — new state: applicant presentation state, per-business employment slots, employed-applicant list.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — new applicant-trigger step, hire/decline/let-go actions, ongoing-cost integration; `resolveIncident`-style applicant chance roll.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — apply passive specialization buffs per-business in `applyIncome` (+ currentReputationPerTurn).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCards.ts` — applicant/specialization skill type definitions (start with existing templates + Town Gossip skill).
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — Town Gossip skill / any new specialization columns if added.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` + `MainStreetAnimator.ts` — new card type walk-on (from left) / walk-off (right) / walk-into-hand animation + SFX.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` / `MainStreetCommands.ts` — hire/decline input + command wiring.
- `tests/main-street/` — unit + browser tests for the mechanic.

## Related work

- CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN — Implement staff peek skill ("Town Gossip" active peek).
- CG-0MSXOXN81004MW8I — Add peek once-per-turn unit tests.
- CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK — Staff specialization: new applicant card suggestions (follow-up, out of scope here).
- CG-0MSQJ7VL9009JHF4 — Group F: Staff abilities beyond hand slots.
- CG-0MS9HJ6AL0087DPB — Engine: ongoingCost for community spaces (same ongoing-cost deduction path).

## Clarifying questions & answers (Appendix)

- Q: How frequently does a staff member apply? — Answer (producer): Per-turn chance computed as `(reputation + income per turn)%`, capped at 15%. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20, recorded in comment CG-C0MT1CHYML001OOU8.
- Q: Are specializations passive or active? — Answer (producer): Passive, always-on buff applied to the business at which they are employed. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: When is the specialization randomized? — Answer (producer): Once per game at start, locked for the full game. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: Which staff pool for applicants? — Answer (producer): Start with existing staff templates; create a follow-up work item for new card suggestions. → Created CG-0MT1CIWSD003VBPK. Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: How is the applicant presented in the UI? — Answer (producer): New card type that walks on from the left, then either walks off to the right (decline) or walks into the hand (hire). Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20.
- Q: What is the specific applicant trigger rate? — Answer (producer): `(Reputation + income per turn)%` capped at 15%. Open detail: the "Town Gossip" example in the original description describes an *active* peek to the top 3 cards of the upcoming deck, which conflicts with the producer's "passive" answer — resolved as passive buff with the active peek delegated to the existing peek skill (CG-0MSXOW6GN008ZSMN). Source: interactive reply 2026-08-20 + item description.

---

- **CG-0MLSDXY9F1FSGQ38** – Coloretto (set-building tableau) (completed)
- **CG-0MSRGUM4P009XRM3** – Upgrade level-up burst on target business (completed)

# Income Phase: phased card-effect animations (coin grids, synergy/rep/event contributions)

**Priority: High** | **Type: Feature** | **Marked for producer review**

## Objective

When the turn ends and the IncomePhase resolves, step through all income card effects one at a time, in a phase-based order and pacing that reads clearly to the player. Starting with base income, each affected business/community-space card shows its income coins "counting out" into a coin grid rendered on the card; then synergy, reputation, event, and upcoming-card contributions either fly coins into that grid or (for negative effects) fly coins out. This replaces the current single-fly-to-HUD collection with a legible, per-contribution breakdown.

## Users & User Stories

- **Player** — "When I end my turn I want to *see* where my income came from — how much each business produced on its own, how much came from synergy and reputation, and how much events changed—so the economy feels legible and satisfying."
- **Player (reduced motion)** — "I still want to follow the phases and see the contributed amounts, but without the coin flights."

## Problem statement

End-of-turn income is currently collapsed into a single coin-per-slot that arcs to the HUD counter (CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE). The player cannot tell how much came from base income vs synergy vs reputation vs event modifiers, which undermines the "watch your town pay out" moment.

## Desired change

Rework the income-collection presentation into a phase-based, per-card coin-grid animation:

1. **Base income "counts out" of each card** — for each producing business/community-space, the card's base income (rounded to nearest 0.5 after this phase) appears as coins (full coin per whole 0.5; half coin for a remainder) that animate out of the card into a coin **grid rendered on the card**. Coins accumulate on the card across phases.
2. **Synergy coins fly in from the synergy line** — coins from the synergy multiplier fly from the synergy line (shared `synergyLineEndpoints` geometry) into the affected card's grid.
3. **Reputation coins fly in from the HUD** — coins from the reputation multiplier fly from the reputation score HUD into the grid.
4. **Event-card effects** — any event card (active duration effects, e.g. Flu Outbreak 0.8×) that affects income flies coins in (boost) or out (reduction) to/from the affected business cards. Duration effects are indicated via animated text lines (see below); single-turn effects just fly the coins.
5. **Upcoming cards** — upcoming cards that affect income either fly coins in, or fly coins out (from the business to the upcoming card, where they disappear).
6. **Grid-to-HUD collection** — at the end of the income step, the accumulated coins on each card's grid fly to the HUD coins counter (reusing/extending the existing fly-to-HUD + final "+total" pop behaviour).

**Coin grid packing (per user):** start as a 5×3 grid; when space runs out, overlap/shrink the coins to fit 10×3, then 15×3, etc. Exact packing "whatever works well" — 3 rows with columns growing (5/10/15...) and shrinking coin size / overlap as needed.

**Rounding (per user, Q8):** each *phase* rounds its own portion to the nearest 0.5 for the coins shown in the grid. The HUD / credited total still uses the exact fractional value (current behaviour preserved).

**Phasing (per user, Q3):** phase-based — all cards show base alongside, then all cards' synergy, then all cards' reputation, then each event, then upcoming-card effects. Each phase lasts ~2–3 seconds. **Reduced motion keeps the phases (same sequence + pacing) but removes the coin animation** (no flights / count-out tweens); the per-phase rounded values still appear.

**Duration-effect text lines (Upcoming panel):** for event cards with a duration, indicate their effect via an animated text line — on a *new* card the effect text animates in one letter at a time with a grow/shrink animation. Then, for each line (new and pre-existing), coins fly to/from the affected business cards. *(The Upcoming-deck-as-face-down-single-card redesign that frees the panel space is a SEPARATE work item — CG-0MSXIQDI4007K6N0 is unrelated (HUD decimals); the deck redesign has no ID yet and is out of scope here.)* This item assumes the panel already has room for these effect lines; if it does not yet, this item proceeds with the best available placement and the deck redesign is tracked separately.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. End-of-turn income walks through phases in order (base → synergy → reputation → events → upcoming), each ~2–3s, with on-card coin grids that accumulate rounded coins per phase (nearest 0.5 per phase).
2. Base coins "count out" of each producing card into its grid; synergy coins fly in from the synergy line; reputation coins fly in from the reputation HUD; event/upcoming effects fly coins in or out to/from the appropriate cards.
3. Grid packing scales from 5×3 to 10×3 to 15×3 by shrinking/overlapping coins as space requires; overflow is visible, not clipped.
4. At the end, grid coins fly to the HUD coins counter with the existing final "+total" pop and coin-pop SFX (extending CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE); the credited HUD total is unchanged (exact fractional total preserved).
5. Duration-effect events show an animated effect line (one-letter grow/shrink reveal for new cards) with coins flying to/from affected businesses; single-turn events just fly coins.
6. Reduced motion keeps the same phases and pacing but strips coin animations (text/phase progression only); replay/headless modes are unaffected (no rendering/audio — documented exemption).
7. New/extended unit + browser tests cover phase ordering, per-phase rounding, grid packing stress (15×3+), event/upcoming fly-in/out, and reduced-motion path.
8. All related documentation updated (code comments, `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`, scene README).

## Constraints

- Presentation-only VFX: never mutates game state, transcript, or turn flow (AGENTS.md rule 8). Must remain non-blocking like the current animation (runs inside the turn-advance window; failures swallowed).
- Reuse existing helpers: `moveGameObject`, `popTextOrIcon`, `SoundManager`/`SFX_KEYS` (`COMMON_SFX_KEYS` convention), `synergyLineEndpoints`, per-slot data from `applyIncome()`/`IncomeResult.breakdown`.
- Respect reduced-motion (SettingsStore / `prefers-reduced-motion`) and headless/replay exemption.
- No new SFX keys unless unavoidable; prefer existing `sfx-coin-pop` etc.
- Must build on / not regress CG-0MSRGTUSK003GDGE (existing fly-to-HUD) and CG-0MSRGUFZ2001ELSR (synergy formation animation).

- `applyIncome()` in `MainStreetAdjacency.ts` returns `IncomeResult.breakdown` (`SlotIncome[]`: `slotIndex`, `businessName`, `baseIncome`, `synergyBonus`, `total`) + `handSynergyTotal`; applies per-slot `income-multiplier` active effects, then the reputation multiplier to the total (exact fractional coins).

- `synergyLineEndpoints()` shared by renderer + animator for synergy-line geometry (p1/p2/mid).
- `ActiveEffect` system (`income-multiplier` / `rep-multiplier`) with `applyActiveEffectMultiplier()`; duration events e.g. Flu Outbreak (0.8×/5 turns), Recession (0.7×/4), Tourist Season (1.15×/3), Labor Shortage (0.9×/3).
- The "Upcoming" panel (`MainStreetRenderer`) shows the incident queue (2 face-up cards + deck) + ⚠ active-effect duration lines.
- HUD geometry mirrors: coins label at `gameW*0.25 + 70`, rep label at strip centre (`gameW*0.5`), `hudY` from layout.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetAnimator.ts` — new `animateIncomePhases()` (or rework `animateIncomeCollection`) implementing the phased coin-grid + fly-in/out sequence; grid-packing helper.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacency.ts` — expose/derive per-slot base/synergy/rep/event contribution breakdown for the phases (likely extend `applyIncome`/`IncomeResult` with richer per-phase data).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — `processEndOfTurn()` / `applyIncome()` — surface per-phase contributions (base, synergy, rep from `applyReputationMultiplier`, event deltas) for the animation.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetDifficulty.ts` — `reputationCoinMultiplier()` — source of the rep-coins fly-in amount.

- **Grid space / readability** — on-card coin grids may visually clutter small card faces; the 5×3→10×3→15×3 overlap/shrink packing may become hard to read at high income. Mitigate: half-coin vs full-coin sizing, controlled overlap, overflow label. (Spike if needed.)

This work item decomposes the upgrade economy fix into 7 child tasks with test-first ordering:

### Phase 1: Unit Tests (test-first, no dependencies)

## Problem statement

Playing an upgrade card currently costs **no action** and never passes through the hand — a market upgrade click applies the upgrade directly to the first eligible business (`buyUpgradeCommand` → `purchaseUpgrade`, no `consumeAction()`). This diverges from the business-card economy (move-to-hand = 1 action, same-day place free, held-card play = 1 action, drag-drop buy-and-place = 1 action + 50% premium) and gives upgrade cards a free second daily action. Upgrades should behave like business cards: go to the hand first when bought by click, with drag-and-drop as the same-turn buy-and-play path.

## Users

- **As a player**, I want playing an upgrade card to consume one of my daily actions like every other purchase/play **so that** the action economy stays honest (1 action/day, 2 with General Manager) and upgrades aren't a free lunch.
- **As a player**, I want upgrades I buy to land in my hand first **so that** I can choose when and where to apply them (target a specific business, possibly next day).
- **As a player**, I want to drag an upgrade straight from the market onto a business when I'm sure **so that** I can buy-and-play in one turn at a +50% premium, exactly like business buy-and-place.
- **As a player**, I want to pick which business to upgrade when playing from hand **so that** I can respond to my current street layout (e.g. branches / multi-level chains).

## Acceptance Criteria (Parent)

- [ ] **Action cost — click path:** Clicking a market upgrade moves it to hand and consumes 1 action; playing the same-day moved upgrade applies it with no additional action; playing a held-from-previous-day upgrade consumes 1 action. All paths decrement actionsRemaining and legality gates reject the action when the budget is spent.
- [ ] **Hand-first + target selection:** Upgrade market cards follow the two-step hand flow — never applied directly from the market on click. When an upgrade is selected in hand, the player clicks an eligible business on the street to apply it; ineligible targets are rejected with illegal-move feedback.
- [ ] **Drag-drop same-turn:** Upgrades in the market are draggable onto eligible street businesses — drag-drop = buy & play in the same turn, consumes 1 action, and charges the +50% premium. Illegal drops snap back with feedback.
- [ ] **Free ops unchanged:** Event cards' free move-to-hand and free play stay free; refresh, sell, hint, discard, community favour, end-turn remain non-action operations.
- [ ] **AI + Monte Carlo:** MainStreetAiStrategy and MainStreetMonteCarlo account for the upgrade action cost in budget-aware valuation, and remain deterministic per seed.
- [ ] **Testing/validation:** New unit tests cover action spend + gating for all three upgrade paths; browser tests cover the hand-first click flow, drag-drop onto eligible/illegal targets, and action-budget dimming; existing upgrade tests updated to the new flow.
- [ ] **Docs:** All related documentation updated; full project test suite (npm test) and npm run build pass.

## Constraints

- Preserve the existing action economy: 1 action/day (2 with General Manager) — upgrades must not create a second implicitly-free action.
- Same-day composite stays free (consistency with business cards); the 50% premium formula must match the business buy-and-place exactly.
- Undo/redo must wrap the new paths (snapshotted commands; new actions after undo invalidate the redo stack).
- State/transcript/save-load fields must stay consistent (e.g. justMovedHandCardId semantics generalise to upgrades; pendingUpgradeIndex-style state added if needed).
- Reduced-motion and mute settings must be respected by any new animation/SFX.

## Effort and Risk

- **Effort:** Medium (37.83h recommended, range [26h-57h])
- **Risk:** Medium (score 10/25, confidence 74%)

## Goal (user story)

As a Main Street player, I want to play a competitive mode against an AI opponent who builds businesses on the **same street**, so that turns give me more to do and the game has a rival to race against.

## Design scope (from feasibility analysis, 2025-07 session)

- **Shared street grid** (10 slots); each placed business is owned by one player; income from a business accrues to its **owner**.
- **Events affect the whole street**: investment events and incidents keep the existing street-wide resolution semantics, but income/damage must be routed per-owner.
- **Staff are player-only**: the AI does not hire staff, and its competitive decision space excludes staff actions (hire-staff, peek).
- **Single shared market row**: buying a card denies it to the opponent (market competition is a first-class feature).
- **Alternating turn structure** — design decision to confirm at intake: alternate MarketPhases within a shared day vs. alternating full days.

## Reusability findings (basis for this item)

- The decision layer (`MainStreetAiStrategy`, `GreedyStrategy`, `scoreAction`, `enumerateLegalActions`, `MainStreetAiPlayer`) transfers ~1:1 — it is UI-free and already shared between the Monte Carlo harness and the hint system.
- The state/engine layers are single-owner: `MainStreetState` has one resourceBank/hand/staffCards/actionsRemaining; `applyIncome`, `resolveEvent`, `resolveIncident`, `computeScore`, `checkEndConditions` all assume one owner. These need a per-player split plus owner-tagged grid slots.
- Greedy heuristics assume the AI owns the whole street (`scoreBusinessAction = (income+synergy)*horizon - cost`; `aiPlanningHorizon` reads a single score) — scoring must become ownership-aware.
- PRD M3 (`docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md`) explicitly scoped "AI vs. player (competitive mode)" as N/A — this item is a deliberate scope extension; note it in the PRD.

## Acceptance criteria (proposed)

- AC1: A competitive-mode state model exists with per-player coins/reputation, hand, staff, action budget and score, plus owner-tagged street slots; deterministic and replayable via seeded RNG.
- AC2: The AI opponent plays a legal full turn through the existing strategy layer (`enumerateLegalActions` → scored choice → `executeAction`), with staff actions excluded.
- AC3: Income accrues to the owner of each business; street-wide events/incidents affect both players under the shared-street semantics.
- AC4: A head-to-head Monte Carlo harness (extending `MainStreetMonteCarlo`) measures the win distribution across >=200 seeds to validate competitive balance.
- AC5 (scene, may be split into a child at planning): competitive mode is selectable from the game selector, renders the shared street with owner colouring, alternates turns, and animates AI turns with SFX per the audio/feedback rule (AGENTS.md best practice 8).

As a developer of the competitive mode, I want the balancing AI's decision layer (`MainStreetAiStrategy` / `GreedyStrategy` / `scoreAction` / `MainStreetAiPlayer`) adapted to shared-street competitive semantics, so the opponent plays competently on a street it does not fully own.

- `scoreBusinessAction` / `scorePlayBusinessFromHandAction` value `(income + synergy) * horizon - cost` with no ownership concept.

- Ownership-aware scoring: evaluate income, synergy, and horizon against the **AI's own** resources/businesses and its own win threshold.
- Staff exclusion: competitive-mode action enumeration drops staff actions from the AI's option space.
- Deterministic validation: extend `MainStreetMonteCarlo` (or a sibling harness) to run head-to-head AI-vs-AI and, where feasible, AI-vs-baseline matches across >=200 seeds; document win/score distributions.

Whether to add opponent-aware *denial* reasoning (blocking the opponent's best slot, buying to deny) — record an explicit in/out decision with rationale; denial can be a follow-up child if in.

- AC1: `scoreAction` and the per-type scoring helpers evaluate placement/upgrade/event value using only the acting player's resources and owned businesses, with the planning horizon computed from the acting player's own score vs. their win threshold.

# Intake Brief: Don't charge for businesses held in the hand

**Problem statement:** Business cards held in the player's hand currently incur ongoing per-turn costs in `applyBusinessOngoingCosts()`. The design intent is that ongoing costs should only apply to business cards placed on the street grid — cards in hand are not yet active and should not incur running costs.

## Users

- **Players:** Business cards they hold but haven't placed yet will no longer drain coins each turn, making the economy more forgiving and strategically cleaner.
- **Balance analysts:** Ongoing costs now only apply to committed tableau investments, aligning with the design intent documented in the GDD.

## User stories

- "As a player, I want to be able to hold business cards in hand without them costing me coins each turn, so I have time to decide when to place them."
- "As a player, I expect only business cards I've actually placed on the street to incur running costs."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Code fix:** `applyBusinessOngoingCosts()` in `MainStreetEngine.ts` only iterates over business cards on `state.streetGrid` — the hand-iteration loop is removed.
2. **Tests updated:** All tests in `tests/main-street/business-ongoing-cost.test.ts` are updated to reflect the new behavior (hand-held cards do not incur ongoing costs; existing tests that asserted hand-based deductions are changed to test street-only or adjusted accordingly).
3. **Documentation:** `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` is updated to reflect that ongoing business costs apply only to cards placed on the street grid (remove references to hand-held costs).
4. **Build passes:** `npm run build` succeeds.
5. **Full test suite passes:** `npm test` succeeds, including all Main Street tests.

## Constraints

- Only the ongoing-cost deduction path changes. The `ongoingCost` field on `BusinessCard` remains populated from CSV data and continues to be displayed in tooltips/card art.
- No UI changes required — the ongoing cost display on cards in hand can remain (it still shows the cost if the card were placed).
- No change to the CSV data or balance parameters.

## Existing state

- `applyBusinessOngoingCosts()` (`MainStreetEngine.ts` line ~1487) iterates over both `state.hand` (business cards) and `state.streetGrid` to sum and deduct ongoing costs.
- `applyStaffOngoingCosts()` only applies to staff cards on the street (no hand equivalent for staff).
- `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts()` only applies to community-space cards on the street grid.
- Documentation in `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` states ongoing business costs apply "whether the card is placed on the street grid or held in hand."
- Tests in `tests/main-street/business-ongoing-cost.test.ts` assert deduction from both hand and street cards.

## Desired change

Remove the hand-iteration block from `applyBusinessOngoingCosts()` so it only processes street-placed business cards, matching the pattern used by `applyStaffOngoingCosts()` and `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts()`.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — `applyBusinessOngoingCosts()`: remove hand-iteration block (lines ~1494-1507)
- `tests/main-street/business-ongoing-cost.test.ts` — Update assertions for street-only deduction
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — Remove "or held in hand" from business cost documentation

## Related work

- **CG-0MSVYPEZ90085SHE** "Main Street: business cards incur ongoing per-turn cost (1/4 purchase price, min 0.25), even in hand" (completed) — introduced the hand-based deduction; this item reverses it.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope is narrow:** Only `applyBusinessOngoingCosts()` changes. No new mechanics, no UI work.
- **Tests need updating:** Multiple test cases in `business-ongoing-cost.test.ts` assert hand-based deductions — these will need to be updated or removed. Risk of missing an edge-case test if not carefully reviewed.
- **CSV data unchanged:** Business cards already have `ongoingCost` populated in CSV for street-placed cards only. No data work needed.
- **No breaking save/load change:** The `ongoingCost` field already exists on `BusinessCard`; only the deduction logic changes.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

# Intake Brief: Main Street — Banked actions not reduced

## Problem statement

Main Street's action-banking mechanic (CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR) folds `bankedActions` into the daily action budget at DayStart but never decrements the banked counter when actions are consumed. The bank therefore never depletes: the HUD shows a stale "(N banked)" count that never drops, and a player at the bank cap (2) keeps a permanent +2 action budget every day — a full-spend day leaves the bank untouched (day-end `bankable = min(actionsRemaining, 1)` yields 0), while a partial-spend day re-banks back toward the cap. The bank acts as an effectively infinite reserve, defeating the "up to two unused turns banked" design intent.

## Users

- **Main Street players** — the banked counter is misleading (shows a reserve that never shrinks), and the exploit lets a player exceed the intended action economy indefinitely (up to 3 actions/day forever instead of banking being a finite reserve).
- **TCE developers / producers** — the engine must enforce banked consumption consistently across the engine `executeAction` path, the command layer, and undo/redo so the mechanic is testable and non-exploitable.

Example user stories:

- "As a player, I want the banked-action counter to decrease by 1 every time I take an action, so the HUD reflects my true reserve."
- "As a player, I want spending my banked reserve to actually deplete it, so banking is a finite strategic resource rather than a permanent bonus."
- "As a developer, I want one enforcement point for action consumption so engine (`executeAction`) and command-layer (`consumeAction`) paths can never diverge."

## Acceptance Criteria

- 1. **Banked decremented on action consumption:** Every action-consuming operation decrements `state.bankedActions` by 1 (floored at 0) alongside `actionsRemaining` — `move-to-hand`, `buy-business`, `play-business-from-hand`, `buy-and-place`, `hire-staff`, and staff-peek — in **both** the engine `executeAction` path and the command-layer `consumeAction` path via a single shared helper (no divergence).
- 2. **Staff actions consume the bank too:** With a General Manager employed (budget = 1 base + 1 GM + 2 banked = 4), taking any action reduces banked by 1, regardless of which budget portion (base/staff/banked) supplied the action — this supersedes the unimplemented "staff consumed first" consumption nuance (AC4 of CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR); day-end banking rules are unchanged.
- 3. **Premium placements don't consume the bank:** The buy-and-place and play-from-hand **premium** paths (+50% coins in place of an action) leave `bankedActions` unchanged — confirmed by operator.
- 4. **Free/non-action operations unchanged:** Community Favour, buy-upgrade, buy/play-event, discard, refresh-market, sell, peek empty-deck no-op, and other free operations do NOT decrement banked.
- 5. **Undo/redo restores banked:** Undoing any action that consumed banked restores the pre-action banked value via the existing command snapshot (which already captures `bankedActions`); verify the premium paths' snapshots too.
- 6. **Day-end banking unchanged:** `bankable = min(actionsRemaining, 1)`, cap 2, staff-never-bank language — unchanged. Net effect: `banked = min(2, (banked − actionsTaken) + bankable)` with floor 0.
- 7. **Tests + validation:** Update the existing `action-banking.test.ts` expectations that encode the buggy behavior (AC3 "4→3→2→1→0" expects banked 2 after spending 2 of 4 → becomes 1; the undo test expects banked unchanged after `executeAction` → becomes `savedBanked − 1` = 0) and add regression tests: banked decrements per action, floors at 0, full-spend day drains the bank, GM games drain too, premium paths untouched, undo restore of banked. Re-baseline Monte Carlo if simulation tests drift (triaged, never silently accepted — CG-0MT4ZHRP5002QMS2 policy). Full `npm test` passes and `npm run build` succeeds.
- 8. **Docs updated:** `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` §Action economy states that banked is consumed 1-per-action as the player acts; HUD action tooltip / i18n copy updated if it misstates consumption (e.g., only if it implies banked survives spending).

## Constraints

- **Main Street only** — no core-engine changes (consistent with CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR).
- Bank cap 2, bank-at-most-1-per-day, day-start composition (`1 + gmBonus + min(2, banked)`) — all unchanged.
- Both consumption paths (engine `executeAction` + command-layer `consumeAction`) must behave identically — centralize into one shared helper; the scene's turn controller dispatches through engine `executeAction` while undo uses the command layer, so a single enforcement point prevents double-decrement.
- Free ops and premium paths must not touch banked (premium replaces the action).
- Tutorial unaffected (TutorialScenario sets `bankedActions: 0` and never banks).

## Existing state

- `state.actionsRemaining` is the single daily counter; `executeDayStart` computes `actionsRemaining = 1 + gmBonus + min(2, bankedActions)` (MainStreetEngine.ts:920-921).
- Action consumption decrements **only** `actionsRemaining`: the `executeAction` switch (MainStreetEngine.ts:269-285: move-to-hand, buy-business, play-business-from-hand, buy-and-place, hire-staff), `peekIncidentDeck` (MainStreetEngine.ts:771), and `consumeAction` (MainStreetCommands.ts:50, used by buy/move/play/hire/buy-and-place commands; premium branches skip it).
- Day-end banking: `bankable = Math.min(state.actionsRemaining, 1)`; `state.bankedActions = Math.min(2, (bankedActions ?? 0) + bankable)` (MainStreetEngine.ts:1036-1039).
- HUD shows `(N banked)` from `state.bankedActions` (MainStreetRenderer.ts:353); tooltip explains "1 action per turn, with up to two turns' unused actions banked" (MainStreetHudTooltips.ts:104).
- Command snapshots already capture and restore `bankedActions` on undo/redo (MainStreetCommands.ts:54, 87-110).

## Desired change

Consume the bank as the player acts: decrement `bankedActions` (floor 0) on every action-consuming operation, via one shared helper used by the engine `executeAction` sites, `peekIncidentDeck`, and the command-layer `consumeAction`. Premium placements and free operations are excluded. Existing tests that assert the buggy non-decrement behavior are updated; regression tests added; Monte Carlo re-baselined if drift occurs.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — add a shared action-consumption helper (decrement `actionsRemaining` + `bankedActions` floor 0; guard `actionsRemaining > 0`); use it at the 5 `executeAction` switch sites (~269-285) and `peekIncidentDeck` (~771); export it for the command layer.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCommands.ts` — `consumeAction` delegates to the shared engine helper; confirm premium branches (`playBusinessFromHandCommand` with premiumCost, `buyAndPlaceBusinessCommand`) still skip consumption.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — §Action economy: document 1-per-action banked consumption.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — tooltip/i18n copy only if it misstates consumption.
- Tests: `tests/main-street/action-banking.test.ts` (update AC3 + undo expectations; add decrement/floor/GM-drain/premium/undo regressions), `tests/main-street/ai-action-budget.test.ts` (verify unaffected), Monte Carlo guardrail tests (`tests/main-street/monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts`, `monte-carlo-greedy-guardrail.test.ts`) — re-baseline on drift per CG-0MT4ZHRP5002QMS2.

## Related work

- **CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR** (completed) — the action-banking implementation this item fixes (consumption side never implemented; AC3's "consumed as the player spends" was unimplemented).
- **CG-0MT4ZHPKN005FEZZ** (completed) — banking mechanics unit test suite (the AC3 test here encodes the buggy expectation).
- **CG-0MT4ZHQF700972P1** (completed) — engine day-end banking / day-start composition (unchanged by this fix).
- **CG-0MT4ZHRP5002QMS2** (completed) — quality gates + Monte Carlo re-baseline policy (drift triaged, never silently accepted).
- **CG-0MT4ZHR9M007VP9D** (completed) — core-rules doc for banking (must be updated to describe consumption).
- **CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P** (open) — tutorial coverage for action banking (semantics it teaches will now match reality).
- **CG-0MT3JMGA60091J8W** (open) — banking-aware AI strategy (will build on corrected semantics).
- **CG-0MSTOF1N5005PK2R** (completed) — base action economy (`actionsRemaining`) this extends.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Monte Carlo / AI baseline drift:** passive AI now depletes banked faster during a game; `monte-carlo-guardrails.test.ts` / `monte-carlo-greedy-guardrail.test.ts` may fail — re-baseline per CG-0MT4ZHRP5002QMS2 policy (drift triaged, never silently accepted).
- **Existing tests encode the bug:** the AC3 and undo tests assert non-decrement; update deliberately, don't weaken.
- **Double-decrement risk:** engine `executeAction` and the command layer both consume in different flows (turn controller uses engine; commands back undo) — a single shared helper prevents double counting; verify no path calls both.
- **Assumption — literal per-action decrement for all budget sources:** operator-confirmed (Q1): every action reduces banked by 1 including staff-supplied actions; GM games fully close the exploit.
- **Assumption — premium replaces the action:** operator-confirmed (Q2): premium placements don't touch banked.
- **Scope-creep risk:** rebalancing the action economy, changing the cap, or redesigning the HUD are out of scope — record as linked work items, do not implement here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 — General Manager interplay: "Does 'banked reduced by 1 per action' apply to every action-consuming operation including the budget portion supplied by staff (GM +1)? Or should banked only decrement after the day's base+staff portion is exhausted (staff-first, which would leave a spend-2/day GM path with the bank at cap forever — i.e. the reported bug would persist for GM games)?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "yes" (literal rule — every action reduces banked by 1, floor 0, regardless of budget source). Source: interactive reply in this session (2026-08-28). Accepted: supersedes the unimplemented "staff consumed first" AC4 of CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR on the consumption side; day-end banking unchanged; existing AC3 test expectation (banked 2 after spending 2 of 4) updates to 1.
- Q2 — Premium placements: "The buy-and-place / play-from-hand premium paths charge +50% coins instead of an action (they skip `consumeAction`). Should banked remain untouched on those?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "confirmed". Source: interactive reply in this session (2026-08-28). Accepted: premium paths leave `bankedActions` unchanged.

When the Monte Carlo guardrail test detects drift from the regression baseline, the current implicit workflow is to regenerate the baseline. This masks real balance shifts and loses the audit trail of what changed.

When a guardrail test fails due to drift:

3. **On operator approval to regenerate:** run `scripts/generate-main-street-monte-baseline.ts` and commit the updated baseline.
4. **On operator choice to investigate:** route to game balance triage (create child work item for balance investigation).

Add a shared action-consumption helper in `MainStreetEngine.ts` that decrements both `actionsRemaining` and `bankedActions` (floor 0), and wire it into all action-consuming paths in the engine and command layer.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Shared helper added:** `consumeAction(state, actionsRemaining, bankedActions)` helper in `MainStreetEngine.ts` that:
   - Decrements `actionsRemaining` by 1 (existing behavior)
   - Decrements `bankedActions` by 1, floored at 0 (new behavior)
   - Guards: only runs when `actionsRemaining > 0`
2. **Engine `executeAction` wired:** The 5 action-consuming switch sites (~line 269-285) — `move-to-hand`, `buy-business`, `play-business-from-hand`, `buy-and-place`, `hire-staff` — call the shared helper instead of decrementing `actionsRemaining` alone.
3. **`peekIncidentDeck` wired:** At ~line 771, replace standalone `actionsRemaining--` with a call to the shared helper.
4. **Command-layer `consumeAction` delegates:** `MainStreetCommands.ts` `consumeAction` delegates to the shared engine helper (imported/exported from engine), ensuring identical behavior between engine path (turn controller) and command path (undo/redo).
5. **Premium paths preserved:** `playBusinessFromHandCommand` with `premiumCost` and `buyAndPlaceBusinessCommand` premium branches still skip consumption (no change to existing behavior).
6. **No double-decrement:** Verify no code path calls both the engine helper and the command-layer `consumeAction` in the same action flow.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — add shared helper (~line 269-285 + ~771), export for command layer
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCommands.ts` — `consumeAction` delegates to shared helper; confirm premium branches skip

## Dependencies

- Blocks: Documentation update (consumes the helper; tests validate behavior)

## Plan

This is a **Small** bug fix with **Medium** risk (Monte Carlo guardrail drift expected). Approval gate requests confirmation due to Medium risk level.

### Proposed decomposition (3 tasks, test-first)

| # | Task | ID | Dependencies |
|---|------|----|--------------|
| 1 | Tests: Update action-banking tests and add regression tests | CG-0MTECTITT0086XLT | None |
| 2 | Implementation: Add shared consumeAction helper and wire into engine/commands | CG-0MTECZMM00043UN6 | Tests (1) |
| 3 | Documentation: Update core-rules doc and HUD tooltip | CG-0MTED0CCC005OQXM | Implementation (2) |

### Rationale

- **Single shared helper** in `MainStreetEngine.ts` prevents double-decrement and ensures engine/commands paths stay identical.
- **Test-first** ensures the buggy expectations are updated before the fix is applied, catching the change in review.
- **Docs last** ensures documentation reflects the final implementation.
- **Monte Carlo re-baselining** is part of the test task — drift is expected (AI depletes banked faster) and will be re-baselined per CG-0MT4ZHRP5002QMS2 policy.

### Vertical slice verification

This is a Small bug fix; vertical phasing is not warranted. Each task is independently verifiable:
- Tests: `npm test` passes (after updating expectations + adding regressions)
- Implementation: `npm test` passes + `npm run build` succeeds
- Docs: No code change, documentation update only

### Risk assessment

- **Monte Carlo drift:** Expected. Re-baselined per policy — not silently accepted.
- **Double-decrement:** Mitigated by single shared helper; no code path calls both engine and command helpers.
- **Existing tests encode the bug:** Deliberately updated — not weakened.
